title: What is an MSME, and should you register as one?
intro: If you run a small or growing business in India, this is probably the single highest-value, lowest-effort thing you can do for it — and it’s free. Here’s what it actually means, whether you qualify, and exactly how to do it.

what.title: What is an MSME?
what.body1: MSME stands for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise — a classification the Government of India uses to extend specific support: easier credit, tax relief, and payment protection that larger businesses don’t get.
what.body2: is the official, free process for getting that recognition.

qualify.title: Do you qualify?
qualify.intro: Classification is based on investment in plant/machinery and annual turnover.
who: Co-operative societies, trusts, and self-help groups
Manufacturing, service, and trading businesses alike

items.title: Collateral-free bank loans
items.detail: Through CGTMSE scheme, government-guaranteed loans are available without needing to pledge property as security.

items.title: Lower interest rates
items.detail: Registered MSMEs qualify for priority-sector lending, offering lower interest rates than commercial bank loans.

items.title: Protection against late payment
items.detail: Under the MSMED Act, buyers are legally required to pay a registered MSME within 45 days.

items.title: Preference in government tenders
items.detail: Central government procurement reserves dedicated quotes for Micro and Small Enterprises.

items.title: Subsidies on growth costs
items.detail: Reduced fees on patent/trademark registration, ISO certification reimbursement, and tech subsidies.

items.title: Tax and compliance concessions
items.detail: Extended MAT credit carry-forward and state-level electricity concessions.

steps.title: How to Register, Step by Step

items.title: Go to the official portal
items.detail: udyamregistration.gov.in — this is the only site you need. Registration is completely free; be cautious of third parties charging a fee.

items.title: Verify with Aadhaar
items.detail: Enter the Aadhaar number of the proprietor (or authorised signatory) and OTP sent to the linked mobile number.

items.title: Verify PAN
items.detail: Enter the business or proprietor’s PAN. The portal validates it automatically.

items.title: Fill in business details
items.detail: Business name, address, bank account & IFSC, NIC activity code, and number of employees.

items.title: Declare investment and turnover
items.detail: These figures determine which category — Micro, Small, or Medium — the business falls into.

items.title: Submit and receive your certificate
items.detail: A Udyam Registration Number (URN) is generated immediately, and the official e-certificate is emailed shortly after.
